learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the physical principles of nuclear energy and can explain and compare the processes of nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.

They know the prerequisites for controlled nuclear fusion and are able to evaluate various realization approaches such as magnetic confinement and inertial confinement regarding their physical and technical feasibility.
Furthermore, they can explain concepts for the construction and functioning of a fusion power plant based on inertial confinement and create a basic energy balance of a fusion reactor.
They have knowledge of the laser technology fundamentals relevant to inertial fusion and understand their technical implementation.
Current technical challenges of fusion research are known to them, and they can critically discuss and evaluate existing solution approaches.
Finally, students are able to reflect on economic and political aspects of nuclear fusion and classify the technology in the context of future energy supply systems.

syllabus_topics: Physical fundamentals of nuclear energy and distinction of energy generation by nuclear fission and nuclear fusion
Technical and physical prerequisites for nuclear fusion as an energy source: especially the Lawson criterion
Realization approaches: inertial confinement and magnetic confinement
Laser technology fundamentals: Basic structure and functioning of lasers, generation of highest pulse energies (megajoule) and powers (petawatt)
Concept of a fusion reactor for generating electrical energy
Economic and political aspects: startups, financing, supply-chain, regulatory aspects
assessment_rules: The examination method (written or oral) will be announced in the first lecture. Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The grade's contribution to the final grade is weighted by ECTS credits.
